name: Otto von der Malsburg to the Hesse-Kassel government, postscripts of f.3 and f.12
date: 1637 (f.3 dated 15 Jan 1637, HCPortal 496; f.12 dated 17 Jan 1637, HCPortal 497)
source: Hessisches Staatsarchiv Marburg, HStAM 4 h Nr. 1411 ("Korrespondenz in Chiffren mit dem Generalkommissar Otto v.d. Malsburg betr. Kriegfuehrung in Muenster und Westfalen"), ff. 3-33. HCPortal records 496-509 (all "Not solved"). See ciphers/malsburg-hessen-1636/NOTES.md for the full intake search log (26 Sept 2026, exit 0).
alphabet: two- and three-digit decimal code groups, dot/space separated as transcribed, plus a handful of plaintext German connective words (e.g. 'Und') and non-numeral marks ('#', a cursive letter 'H') left en clair inside the numeral stream

leaf_ids: hstam_4_h_1411_0003 (f.3, postscript below the signature, HCPortal 496)
constraints.nomenclator_flag: K=95 with 27/95 singletons at N=352 (K/N=0.27) is above the ~60-distinct-with-many-singletons heuristic in the brief: treat as a nomenclator/code+mark design, not a plain substitution cipher, until shown otherwise
constraints.reconciliation: pass A/B blind Sonnet transcriptions of both leaves (bMAL2), reconciled against the crops (bMAL3, 26 Sept 2026): f.3 raw agreement 174/194=89.7%, f.12 153/159=96.2%; disagreements.tsv settled from the image (26/26 rows opened, 23 settled H, 1 merged two-token misread into a single blotted 3-digit token at M, 2 left M/unsettled under a water/ink stain on f.3 line 7 (crop hstam_4_h_1411_0003_L30_s1.jpg, cols 12-13) -- genuinely illegible at 12x zoom, not guessed. f.12 lines L39-L43 (5 of an 11-line block) and a third cipher passage in a different hand/alphabet marked 'cifrat cela' are untranscribed, out of this job's scope (bMAL2 NOTES.md).

cheap_tests_in_order: 1. IC and sign-frequency profile of the reconciled numeral stream vs German plain (de16 corpus) and vs matched masc/homophonic controls at N=352, K=95 -- this job (bMAL3).

2. If test 1 does not resolve it: fetch and reconcile the remaining eight HCPortal records (502-509) on this fond to pool the corpus above the 2,000-sign sign-pool threshold (CLAUDE.md's pools-first selection rule) before a from-scratch cryptanalytic attack, since a single ~350-sign postscript is short for a nomenclator with this many distinct codes.

judge.era_note: judge.language='de' resolves through tools/judge_plaintext.py's LANG_CORPORA to tools/data/de16/composed_enhg.txt, i.e. de16 = Early New High German (15th-16th c.). This target is a 1637 chancery/military letter, roughly a century later than de16's register and 250+ years earlier than the only other German corpus on file (de20 = 1880-1940 prose, tools/data/de20). Neither corpus is era-matched; de16 is used as the closer of the two available (CLAUDE.md rule 3's pt17/pt18/es17c corpus-era lesson) and any FAIL/PASS here should be treated as a de16-register verdict, not a verdict on 1637 chancery German specifically, until a 17th-century German corpus is built.
